prompts: Users of our harness plugins report that tool.after hooks run out of order, that sometimes a hook never runs, and that a failing hook is silently ignored. The hook bus and the plugin are in {WS}; the README there says how the bus must behave. Fix the bus. Its public API stays as it is, the tests in {WS}/test stay as they are, and package.json takes no dependencies.
answers:
[goal] Fix the hook bus so `tool.after` hooks run in order, always run, and propagate failures, per the README contract.

[action] Rewrote `HookBus.emit` in `src/bus.ts`. The old code was:

```ts
list.forEach(async (handler) => { await handler(payload); });
```

`forEach` does not await async callbacks, so all handlers started at once (out of order), `emit` resolved immediately (before any handler settled), and handler rejections became unhandled promise rejections (silently ignored). The fix:

```ts
const list = [...(this.handlers.get(event) ?? [])];
for (const handler of list) {
  await handler(payload);
}
```

The snapshot copy implements the README rule that an emit runs the handlers subscribed when it started, so a mid-emit unsubscribe (like the plugin's one-time notice handler) doesn't disturb the in-flight emit.

[result]
- `npm test`: 2 pass, 0 fail (existing tests untouched).
- A temporary script (removed after) verified the full README contract against the fixed bus: sequential start/finish order across an async handler; `emit` not resolving before handlers settle; a rejecting handler rejecting `emit` with the same error and skipping later handlers; mid-emit self-unsubscribe not stopping other handlers in that emit; and the audit plugin end-to-end — notice exactly once, redaction applied before the audit log entry, log showing `password=[redacted]`. All passed.
- Public API unchanged (`on`, `emit`, `count`), no dependencies added, no files touched outside `src/bus.ts`. No browser tabs or apps were opened.

[assumptions] The README is the contract (it says "how the bus must behave"); the plugin was correct and only needed a correct bus; the two existing tests are the only required tests, so I verified the rest with a throwaway script rather than adding tests to `./test`.

[how I know it is right] Each reported symptom maps to a verified check: out-of-order → check 1 (sequential), never runs → the plugin's audit entry now appears with redacted output (check 5), silently ignored failure → check 3 (emit rejects with the same error, later handlers skipped).
